blocks.text: The input domain includes more than an element type. Does the caller retain exclusive control of the vector while the function reads it? May the function allocate? Is the result needed before the next reading arrives? Is there a bound on retained observations? Here the algorithm assumes an already constructed, stable, finite vector and performs a synchronous read. It does not accept a concurrently changing stream. That boundary prevents a later claim that the same function is automatically safe for an acquisition thread.

blocks.text: An index is a description of a position in a particular sequence state. It does not own that sequence. Returning an integer avoids a dangling pointer from the function itself, but the integer can become semantically stale if the caller inserts at the front before using it. A result type solves one problem; it does not solve every lifetime and identity problem. When a result must survive reordering, return a stable record identifier or an owned copy under a different contract.

topics.title: 1.2.2 Reasoning with Invariants
topics.summary: Before iteration i, the invariant is: best is the earliest maximum position in the prefix [0, i). It holds initially at i = 1 because the one-element prefix contains only index zero. If the new value is larger, replacing best extends the invariant; if it is equal or smaller, retaining the old index preserves both maximality and earliest occurrence.

cards.question: Explain Reasoning with Invariants in your own words.
cards.answer: Before iteration i, the invariant is: best is the earliest maximum position in the prefix [0, i). It holds initially at i = 1 because the one-element prefix contains only index zero. If the new value is larger, replacing best extends the invariant; if it is equal or smaller, retaining the old index preserves both maximality and earliest occurrence.

blocks.text: Use three proof obligations. Initialization: before the first iteration the prefix has one element, so its sole position is the earliest maximum. Preservation: the next value is either larger, equal, or smaller. A larger value becomes the unique best among the expanded prefix; an equal or smaller value leaves the earlier best valid. Exit: when i == n, the prefix is the whole sequence. These arguments describe a relationship between state and input, rather than a list of observed test outputs.

blocks.text: Termination is a separate obligation. During the loop, n - i is a nonnegative count of unprocessed elements, and each iteration reduces it by one. The subtraction is justified only while i <= n; that fact belongs to the loop’s range reasoning. With a stable finite vector, the count reaches zero. Changing the vector’s size while iterating would invalidate this particular proof even before considering C++ iterator rules.

focus.title: Maintain the largest-so-far rule
focus.code: int maximum(const std::vector<int>& v){ int best=v.at(0); for(std::size_t i=1;i<v.size();++i) if(v[i]>best) best=v[i]; return best; }
explain: const vector<int>& v borrows the caller’s vector without modifying it. at(0) checks the first index. The loop starts at 1, uses < to stop before size(), increments i, and replaces best only when the next value is larger. return sends the answer back.
focus.what: After each completed iteration, best is the maximum of the values visited so far.
focus.where: The function is defined before main calls it. The scan itself runs at execution time.
focus.why: One pass is enough; sorting would do extra work and change the input order.
focus.invariant: The input must be nonempty for a successful result. best must be a value from the visited prefix.
focus.risk: Starting best at zero gives a wrong result for all-negative input. Replacing < with <= reads beyond the vector at the last iteration.

focus.title: Check the example trace
explain: The brace list constructs a temporary vector from 4, 9, 2, 7. It stays alive through this call, so the borrowed const reference is valid. The returned integer is sent to cout, then a newline.
focus.what: The trace is best=4, then 9, then 9, then 9.
focus.where: The temporary input is destroyed after the full expression finishes.
focus.why: This small fixture makes the scan’s invariant easy to check before using larger inputs.
focus.invariant: The final output is 9. The function returns an integer value, not a reference to a temporary.
focus.risk: Returning a reference to a local best would produce a dangling reference once the function returns.
